Definition: from G1909 and G906; to throw upon (literal or figurative, transitive or reflexive; usually with more or less force); specially (with G1438 implied) to reflect; impersonally, to belong to:--beat into, cast (up-)on, fall, lay (on), put (unto), stretch forth, think on.
BiblicalUsage: Epiballo means to throw upon, to lay on, to cast — hands laid on Jesus in the garden, hands laid on the apostles, a patch laid on an old garment, a thought laid on the heart. It is the word for what is put onto something else, whether violence or repair.
TheologicalSignificance: Hands that seize and hands that heal are not the same, though the word is the same. I believe the gospel is the story of the second kind winning: the hands laid on Jesus in violence became, in His own hands, the laying on of life.
